to.text:
- When a task's required target is missing because it is neither visible nor held, do not repeatedly cycle among the same small set of already-checked locations; after a checked location yields no target, choose a different candidate location for the next move.
- On the next search move, choose an admissible candidate that is not the current location and not one of the locations visited in the last two pre-action observation/action pairs; when a candidate not yet inspected in those observations is available, choose it rather than a recently checked location.
- If the current or recent location is an empty container, choose an admissible instance of the same container type whose name is not in the recent history when available, or a different visible container/surface type before returning to the same checked set.
- Include all plausible visible surfaces and furniture in the candidate set, such as dining tables, desks, beds, sidetables, countertops, shelves, and the named destination surface, as well as remaining closed containers; do not assume the target cannot be on the destination surface.
- Apply this missing-target search expansion to both single-instance and multi-instance target tasks, not only while a multi-instance task remains unmet.
- Do not repeatedly alternate between two or more already-checked locations; if the last two search moves were to already-checked locations and plausible unchecked candidates remain, choose an unchecked candidate or open a newly reached closed container from the admissible actions before any return to a checked location.
- Preserve the existing collection exception: when a known location still contains a needed target instance, return to it as required by the collection guidance even if it appears in the recent history; this exception overrides the recent-location exclusion.

- When a task's required target is missing because it is neither visible nor held, do not repeatedly cycle among the same small set of already-checked locations; after a checked location yields no target, choose a different candidate location for the next move.
- On the next search move, choose an admissible candidate that is not the current location and not one of the locations visited in the last two pre-action observation/action pairs; when a candidate not yet inspected in those observations is available, choose it rather than a recently checked location.
- If the current or recent location is an empty container, choose an admissible instance of the same container type whose name is not in the recent history when available, or a different visible container/surface type before returning to the same checked set.
- Include all plausible visible surfaces and furniture in the candidate set, such as dining tables, desks, beds, sidetables, countertops, shelves, and the named destination surface, as well as remaining closed containers; do not assume the target cannot be on the destination surface.
- Apply this missing-target search expansion to both single-instance and multi-instance target tasks, not only while a multi-instance task remains unmet.

- When a task requires a hot or cool target and the target is held, perform the required heat/cool transformation at the appropriate appliance using the direct heat/cool action before moving the target into any container or final receptacle.
- If the final receptacle is itself a thermal appliance such as a microwave or fridge, do not treat opening it, moving the target into it, and closing it as satisfying the required transformation; after transforming the held target, place it directly in the final receptacle.
- Do not apply the opposite thermal transformation at the final receptacle after the required heated or cooled state has been achieved; the destination appliance's role in placement does not require the reverse heat/cool command.
- Preserve the successful direct-transformation pattern: cool or heat the target while holding it at the appropriate appliance, then carry it to the destination and place it without a redundant thermal round trip.
